title: Persian Lamb Stew (Khoresh)
subtitle: saffron-scented lamb with dried limes
excerpt: Lamb shoulder slow-cooked with yellow split peas, saffron, and dried limes until the meat is falling-apart tender. The dried limes give the broth a sour, floral depth that is unlike anything else.
sourceNotes: Khoresh refers to a class of Persian slow-cooked stews eaten over rice. This style of cooking has been central to Persian cuisine for more than a thousand years.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the batch and freeze half.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Tastes better the next day. Reheat gently.

content.text: Bloom the saffron in a little hot water before adding it. This releases the colour and flavour. Pierce the dried limes before adding them -- this lets the bitterness infuse into the broth gradually.

items.prepNote: cut into large chunks, bone in if possible
use 2 dried limes (loomi), pierced -- or use juice of 1 lemon

content.text: Bloom the saffron in 3 tbsp of hot water and set aside.
Brown the lamb pieces in butter over high heat in a large pot. Do this in batches. Set aside.
Fry the onion in the same pot for 8 minutes until golden. Add the turmeric and cinnamon. Stir for 1 minute.
Return the lamb to the pot. Pour in the lamb stock. Add the pierced dried limes and the saffron water.
Bring to a boil. Skim the foam. Reduce heat and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the yellow split peas. Continue simmering for 45 minutes until the peas are soft and the lamb is tender.
Remove the dried limes. Season with salt. Serve over saffron-infused basmati rice.

items.cause: Dried limes left in too long or too many added
items.fix: Remove the dried limes earlier. Taste as you go. One or two limes is usually enough for a 4-person batch.

items.cause: Old dried peas or added too early
items.fix: Older pulses take longer to cook. Keep simmering with the lid on and add a splash more stock if needed.

items.cause: Not bloomed long enough or too little saffron
items.fix: Allow the saffron to steep in the hot water for at least 10 minutes before adding. Use good-quality saffron threads.

content.text: Khoresh is a category of Persian stew eaten over rice across Iran. These slow-cooked dishes have been central to Persian cooking for more than a thousand years. Dried limes, or loomi, are a hallmark ingredient in Persian and Iraqi cooking. They are available in Middle Eastern grocers and online. This style of khoresh is popular in the south and south-west of Iran.
